suggestions: Require dual-horizon agreement on risk-adjusted trend quality before volume weighting: replace the single Pct(close,60)/Std(Pct(close,1),120) term with Min(Pct(close,20)/Std(Pct(close,1),60), Pct(close,60)/Std(Pct(close,1),120)) (or average only when both share the same sign). Investment rationale: a lone 60-day Sharpe-like score is often dominated by a recent burst or mean-reversion episode embedded in the window, so IC flips sign across blocks (block_pos_frac=0.5) even when volume expansion looks stable; forcing short- and long-horizon risk-adjusted trends to agree keeps exposure to genuinely persistent drifts and filters window-boundary artifacts that drive RankIC variance, directly targeting RankIR without reusing the prior price–volume correlation dual-horizon gates.

Replace the discrete time-series Rank on relative volume with a continuous, volatility-normalized participation measure: use Ma(Log(volume)/Ma(Log(volume),120), 20) / Ma(Std(Log(volume),40), 20) (or Ts_Zscore of Ma(volume,20)/Ma(volume,120) over 120 days) instead of Rank((Ma(volume,60)/Ma(volume,120)),120). Investment rationale: Ts_Rank on the volume ratio creates step jumps whenever a name crosses its historical percentile band, which reshuffles cross-sectional ordering day-to-day and inflates evaluation turnover (0.95) despite moderate portfolio turnover; a smoothed log-volume level scaled by its own variability preserves graded participation intensity and rank continuity, dampening idiosyncratic reordering that degrades RankIR and out-of-sample RankIR (rank_ir_valid=-0.14).

Apply exponential temporal decay to the composite before cross-sectional standardization and compress tails with a time-series ordinal transform: Ewm(Ma((Pct(close,60)/Std(Pct(close,1),120))*w, 10), 0.15) followed by Ts_Rank(..., 120) and a mild cross-sectional Rank (rather than Zscore(...,120) on raw levels). Investment rationale: equal-weight Ma(60) plus level-based Zscore over 120 days overreacts to outlier Sharpe-like spikes and boundary rolloffs in the moving window, producing unstable quintile membership and weak validation IC; EWM gives smoother signal evolution across regimes, while Ts_Rank converts each stock’s own history into a persistent relative score that limits tail-driven rank scrambles—improving year_pos_frac and RankIR consistency without repeating the prior short Ma(5) smoothing on correlation products or the monotonicity-focused Rank(Ts_Rank) stack on signed correlation gates.
